newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila sees Burma joining ASEAN before year 2000.
newsitem.headline: Manila sees Burma joining ASEAN before year 2000.

text.p: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) expects Burma, Laos and Cambodia to join the grouping before the year 2000, Philippine President Fidel Ramos said on Monday.

"We now expect ASEAN to complete uniting the natural cluster of 10 southeast Asian countries well before the turn of the century," Ramos told a seminar on ASEAN security and the role of external powers in preserving regional peace.
ASEAN leaders agreed at an informal summit in Jakarta over the weekend that observer nations Burma, Laos and Cambodia would be granted full membership simultaneously but did not say when.

Ramos said the expansion of ASEAN, which groups Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, the Philippines, Singapore, Brunei and Vietnam, to include the three countries would augur well for southeast Asia's future.
"None of our countries can stand up separately to the intense competition of the global economy and the power politics that might yet embroil the Asia-Pacific of the future," he said.
"But united we can face outside presures and shape our future according to our collective aspirations."
